packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-07 - unverified image-only reading

EXPOSURE / RULES
No proposed identification or prior reading was present in my context. I opened only PROMPT.md and the four image files of this packet. No web, search, catalogue or edition was used.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
Four images: image-001 = overview of one face (with ruler), image-002 = close tile of that face; image-003 = overview of the other face, image-004 = close tile of it. The tiles are small (c. 700 px wide), so the letters are only a few pixels high; this limits the reading more than the state of the leaf does on face A.
The fragment is a small scrap, about 5 cm wide by about 3.5 cm high by the ruler, with a straight top and side cuts and a torn lower edge. A small tab of yellowish material (paper or adhesive) sticks out at one upper corner.
Face A (image-001/002): the top c. 40% is blank margin; below it are five lines of a small, compressed, heavily abbreviated book hand in dark brown/black ink, arranged in TWO COLUMNS with an intercolumnar space: the left column preserves nearly a full column width (its left edge is slightly cut), the right column only its first 4-7 letters per line. So this is the top of a two-column page (upper margin plus the first five lines of both columns). Red is used for a paragraph mark or small initial: one at the start of right-column line 3, and a red-touched letter after a vertical stroke in left-column line 2. In the upper margin are four or five groups of much larger, bolder letters written at 90 degrees to the text (reading vertically), partly faint; they look like offset or a separate inscription in a larger script, not part of the main text (tentative). A further faint vertical group lies at the right edge.
Face B (image-003/004): same layout seen from the back: blank upper margin, then five lines; here the left part is the line-ends of one column (4-7 letters) and the right part is nearly a full column. Ink much paler and rubbed, with a dark grey smudge over the right third. Thin vertical strokes inside the lines (after the first word group of line 1, and mid-line in lines 2-3) look like dividing strokes/paragraph marks in ink.
No running title, no rubric heading, no interlinear gloss visible. Tentative interpretation: continuous prose in a scholastic-type abbreviated hand; the vertical strokes followed by a capital suggest short units (verses, lemmata or sentences) marked off within the line. Not confirmed.

FACE A - TRANSCRIPTION (image-002; lines counted from the top of the tile, the vertical marginal inscription not counted)

Upper margin, written sideways, large letters (left to right across the margin; each group reads vertically):
  group 1: n . 9(?)   [or "n . s"]
  group 2: p(?)i[.]m(?)   [a letter with descender followed by minims]
  group 3: t(?)iiii(?)  [mostly minims]
  group 4: g(?)a(?) / q(?)[.]
  group 5 (at right edge, faint): [illegible]

Left column:
image-002 line 1: [.]nel(?) visiōe(?) fuit m(?)irata(?) sui(?)
image-002 line 2: [..]ersus(?) | V'z(?) q(uod)(?) ab eo luca(?)      (vertical stroke after the first word; the V is touched with red)
image-002 line 3: [...]z(?) sp̄e(?) . s(?) . gr̄(?) 7 fecūdit'(?)
image-002 line 4: [..]uiso(?) . s(?) . gr̄t'l(?) unc(?) uiues(?)
image-002 line 5: [..] unc'(?) v'g(?)[..] . [..] sc̄is(?)       (lower parts of letters lost in the tear)

Right column (line beginnings only):
image-002 line 1: con(?)[...]
image-002 line 2: steph's(?)[...]      (or "strph's"; a word beginning st- with p and a suspension)
image-002 line 3: [red paragraph mark or red initial] ex(?) tu(?)[...]     (possibly "Q" or "D" in red followed by "eꝯ"/"ex")
image-002 line 4: go(?) l'agu(?)[...]      (or "qo lagu-")
image-002 line 5: [..]t(?) sim(?)[...]      (or "sicut"; truncated by tear)

FACE B - TRANSCRIPTION (image-004)

Left part (line ends of one column):
image-004 line 1: [...]lu(?) p(?)[..]
image-004 line 2: [...]uientia(?)      (or "-menda"/"-mencia"; minims)
image-004 line 3: [...]c(?)ro(?) . eld(?)
image-004 line 4: [...]cl(?)uus(?) se(?)
image-004 line 5: [...]n(?)[...]

Right part (nearly full column):
image-004 line 1: i(?) [..]ue(?)[.]udo(?) | So(?) p(?)tiue'(?) co(?)[...]      (vertical stroke before "So"/"fo"; this second half is the darkest writing on the face)
image-004 line 2: dyo(?) . i(?) c(?)e[..]o(?) aug(?) | [...]
image-004 line 3: y(?) p(?)ri[..]p(?)i(?) | z(?)[.]n(?)[...]
image-004 line 4: h(?) c(?)ret(?) h(?)[..] . p(?) p(?)[...]
image-004 line 5: co(?)n(?) uidet'(?) | [..]dicit(?)[...]      (truncated by tear)

SELECTION AND WHAT REMAINS UNREAD
The whole surviving text was attempted (5 lines x 2 columns per face); nothing was skipped. There is no span of ten lines on this scrap: only five lines survive per face.
Confidence: face A left column is the only reasonably legible area, and even there every word carries a query; the firmest letter groups are "fuit" (line 1), "ab eo luca-" (line 2), a tironian "7" followed by a word beginning "fec-" (line 3), and, in the right column, a word beginning "steph-" (line 2). Face B is essentially unread: the words given are shapes, not readings.

LIMITATIONS
- The supplied tiles are low resolution (about 700 x 470 px for the whole scrap); a native-resolution or macro image of both faces would very probably allow face A to be read securely and would improve face B.
- Lines are cut at the left of face A's left column (1-2 letters) and after the first few letters of its right column; the reverse holds on face B.
- Line 5 on both faces is cut through by the torn lower edge.
- Face B is rubbed and smudged grey on its right third.
- Which face is recto is not determinable; if face A is the recto, its two columns are a/b and face B's are c/d (line ends of c, most of d), and vice versa.
- The sideways large letters in the upper margin of face A may be offset from another leaf; I could not read them as words.
- Unverified image reading.
